questions.q: Why does a typical firewall or IDS alert require judgment from an analyst?
options: Because the traffic it evaluates could legitimately be either benign or malicious
Because firewalls are never able to log any traffic details
Because IDS signatures only fire on traffic from honeypots
Because analysts are required to re-verify every rule weekly
questions.explain: A spike in traffic or an odd login could have an innocent explanation, so an analyst has to add context before judging it malicious.

questions.q: What is the real reason a honeypot alert has such a low false-positive rate?
options: Because nothing legitimate should ever touch it, so there is no innocent explanation available for the alert
Because honeypots use more advanced encryption than firewalls
Because honeypots are monitored by more analysts than firewalls
Because honeypot alerts are generated less frequently than firewall alerts
questions.explain: A honeypot alert reports a fact that is already bad by construction, unlike a firewall alert that might still be legitimate traffic.

questions.q: What is the real limitation of honeypots and deception technology described in this lesson?
options: They only catch attackers who happen to interact with the decoy — they provide no visibility into traffic that never touches it
They generate more false positives than any other security tool
They cannot be used alongside firewalls or IDS systems
They require constant manual reconfiguration to remain effective
questions.explain: An attacker who never touches the decoy walks right past it undetected, since a honeypot only sees what actually reaches it.

questions.q: Why is a honeypot alert still considered valuable despite firing rarely?
options: Because when it fires, it can be trusted immediately without the investigation a firewall or IDS alert would need first
Because it automatically blocks every attacker on the network
Because it replaces the need for any other detection tool entirely
Because rare alerts are always weighted more heavily by compliance auditors
questions.explain: A single confirmed honeypot hit can be worth more than many noisy alerts, because it doesn't need investigating to be believed, only to be acted on.

questions.q: What role does deception technology play in an overall detection strategy, according to this lesson?
options: One trustworthy layer that catches lateral movement other tools often miss, not a replacement for comprehensive coverage
The single tool that should replace firewalls, IDS, and EDR entirely
A tool used only for compliance reporting, not actual detection
A tool that eliminates the need for any human analyst review
questions.explain: Deception technology supplies a small number of highly trustworthy alerts, complementing rather than replacing the rest of a detection program.
